name: og-res-nitrogen-assimilation
title: The Nitrogen Bottleneck
question: Carbon fixation is not the only requirement for a protocell. Can an FeS-mediated vent reduce the early ocean's oxidised / inert nitrogen (NO3-/NO2-/N2) to ammonium fast enough to keep pace with carbon fixation, and which conditions (FeS activity, nitrate supply, temperature) decide whether nitrogen becomes limiting first?
hypothesis: On an Fe/Ni/S catalyst with an H2 reductant, nitrate is reduced through nitrite to ammonium and drawn into amino-acid precursors by reductive amination; reduced N keeps pace with reduced carbon (C:N supply ratio near Redfield) only inside a bounded region of (nitrate supply x FeS activity), and outside it — low feed or passivated mineral — the C:N ratio blows up and nitrogen, not carbon or energy, becomes the first limiting resource.
objective: Add nitrogen as its own module (FeS-mediated NO3-/NO2- -> NH4+ with minor N2 fixation and carbon-demanded reductive amination), track the C:N supply ratio, and map the region where reduced-N production keeps pace with the carbon-fixation demand.
result: All six tests pass — the favourable arm sustains ~1.0 mM ammonium and a C:N supply ratio of ~5.0 (reduced N keeps pace with carbon), nitrogen mass is conserved to machine precision (residual ~1e-20 M), ammonium collapses to <1 µM in both the no-FeS and no-H2 controls, and a scarce nitrate feed drives C:N from ~5 to ~47 (nitrogen becomes limiting first).

findings.statement: FeS-mediated reduction of nitrate through nitrite sustains a standing ammonium pool (~1.0 mM) with an H2 reductant at ~80 C, the first reduced nitrogen the chemistry needs.

evidence.observed: settled NH4+ ~1.0 mM; peak production ~2.0e-5 mol/s

findings.explanation: A real ReducedNitrogenProductionProcess reduces NO3- -> NO2- -> NH4+ gated by H2 availability, an FeS temperature window and catalyst activity.

findings.statement: At the favourable operating point reduced-N production keeps pace with the carbon-fixation demand — the C:N supply ratio settles at ~5.0, within the viable (near-Redfield) band.
findings.explanation: The C:N supply ratio = carbon demand / reduced-N production; reductive amination draws ammonium into amino-acid precursors at a rate set by the carbon demand.

findings.statement: Ammonium is present only with BOTH an active FeS catalyst and an H2 reductant — it collapses to <1 µM when either is removed (each is necessary, not merely correlated).

evidence.observed: favourable NH4+ ~1.0 mM; no-FeS and no-H2 controls <1 µM

findings.statement: A parameter sweep over (nitrate supply x FeS activity) maps where reduced N keeps pace with carbon versus where nitrogen becomes limiting FIRST. Reduced N keeps pace only where the nitrate feed is sufficient AND the mineral is active; starving the feed drives the settled C:N supply ratio from ~5 to ~47 (nitrogen limiting), so the decision is a bounded region, not a representative run.

evidence.observed: favourable C:N ~5.0 (keeps pace) vs scarce-nitrate C:N ~47 (limiting); keeps-pace boundary at C:N = 8

findings.explanation: 16x16 sweep of the real open-flow reduced-nitrogen reactor (nitrate supply 2e-6-1e-4 M/s x FeS activity 0.05-1.0) reduced to the settled C:N supply ratio + a keeps-pace mask, rendered as the nitrogen phase map (Decision view). Runner sims/compute_nitrogen_grid.py.

findings.statement: Nitrogen mass is conserved by construction — every internal reaction conserves N atoms, so the per-step accounting residual stays at ~1e-20 M (the matter-accounting invariant).

report.title: (Module I) — nitrogen as a limiting resource
report.verdict: PASS — reduced N keeps pace in a bounded region; nitrogen limits first outside it
report.main_insight: FeS-mediated nitrate reduction supplies ammonium fast enough to keep pace with carbon (C:N ~5) only where the nitrate feed is sufficient AND the mineral is active; outside that region nitrogen is the first limiting resource.
report.conclusion: Reduced nitrogen is a viable co-requirement with reduced carbon inside a bounded (nitrate supply x FeS activity) region; the campaign must carry nitrogen supply, not only carbon, as a gating resource.
report.caveat: Reduction kinetics are lab-motivated (Doerr FeS N2-fixation yields are low; nitrate-reduction rates are calibrated so the favourable arm approaches a standing mM pool), and the C:N keeps-pace band is a Redfield-like first-principles target, not a Hadean measurement.

conclusion: Reduced-nitrogen production reproduces an FeS-mediated ammonium source and maps the region where it keeps pace with carbon fixation; nitrogen becomes limiting first where the nitrate feed is scarce or the mineral is passivated. Supplies reduced N (ammonium + amino-acid precursors) to the downstream protometabolism and heredity stages.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces an FeS-mediated reduced-nitrogen source with the controls behaving correctly (no FeS or no H2 => no ammonium).

explanatory_gain.basis: The C:N supply ratio explains WHEN nitrogen rather than carbon or energy becomes the first limiting resource, as a bounded region in (nitrate supply x FeS activity).

limitations: FeS nitrate-reduction and N2-fixation kinetics are lab-motivated, not first-principles surface kinetics; Doerr-2003 N2 fixation is deliberately a minor source.
The phase map sweeps (nitrate supply x FeS activity) in the open-flow regime; temperature, H2 and the carbon demand are held fixed (facets, not yet swept).
The keeps-pace C:N band is a Redfield-like biomass target; the true early-cell C:N requirement is uncertain.

resolved_uncertainties: A viable reduced-N source exists on FeS; ammonium strictly requires both the mineral catalyst and the H2 reductant.
The (nitrate supply x FeS activity) region where reduced N keeps pace with carbon is now mapped (16x16 sweep, open-flow sustained C:N), not inferred from a single run.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether reduced N or reduced carbon is the tighter constraint under joint (coupled) limitation — here the carbon demand is an exogenous parameter, not the live og-01/og-02 carbon flux.
The continuous temperature / H2 dependence of the keeps-pace boundary (held fixed in this sweep).

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Couple the reduced-nitrogen reactor's c_demand to the live og-01/og-02 net carbon flux and co-limit

literature_anchors.model_observable: ammonium production on FeS vs controls
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Met qualitatively — the FeS-mediated route produces ammonium only with an active mineral and an H2 reductant; N2 fixation is modelled as a deliberately minor source alongside the dominant nitrate-reduction route.

literature_anchors.expectation: Native-metal / mineral catalysis drives reductive prebiotic chemistry toward amino-acid precursors
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Met — reductive amination draws ammonium into an amino-acid-precursor pool at a rate set by the carbon-fixation demand (the C:N coupling).

implemented_methods: Module I (kinetics) — REAL ReducedNitrogenProductionProcess: FeS-catalysed NO3- -> NO2- -> NH4+ gated by H2 availability, an FeS temperature window and catalyst activity, with a minor abiotic N2-fixation source (Doerr-2003) and carbon-demanded reductive amination toward amino-acid precursors. Open-flow nitrate feed + ammonium washout give a condition-dependent sustained steady state.
C:N supply-ratio accounting — carbon demand / reduced-N production is the decision observable; nitrogen mass is conserved by construction (per-step residual ~1e-20 M).
Decision surface — 16x16 sweep over (nitrate supply x FeS activity) reduced to the settled C:N supply ratio + keeps-pace mask, persisted to artifacts/ and rendered as the nitrogen phase map.

key_assumptions: Reduced nitrogen (NH4+) is a hard co-requirement with reduced carbon; the early ocean's accessible N is oxidised (NO3-/NO2-) or inert (N2).
The useful decision observable is the C:N SUPPLY ratio (production vs demand), not any single pool.
expert_questions: RESOLVED: nitrogen is built as its OWN module (not folded into carbon fixation), with the C:N supply ratio as the decision observable and FeS activity / nitrate supply as the controlling axes.
